metadata.remarks: Supersedes assessment result 1f1e64d4-4c2e-4165-9a9e-1e41b6d25dbd, which went stale on 2026-09-19 when #30 made the UUIDv5 key grammar normative and tripped the early-staleness trigger for a federation change affecting peer verification, deduplication, or the UUID key grammar. That firing was recorded rather than re-attested at the time, so r2 read as stale in that area until this revision. The superseded record is kept unmodified. Its recorded hash 5285d3d660acd900337ade9a90d609fc91704215910f75cabc89abc35707638d identifies the revision of threat-model.md it actually reviewed; that revision lives in git history, which is an immutable store here because main requires verified signatures. Editing a superseded record would break the only link back to what was reviewed, so it is never edited. This revision also records the cadence rule that governs when the next re-issue happens — see the Freshness section of the threat model, and issue #31.

import-ap.remarks: There is no separate assessment plan. The requirement, its scope and its evidencing method are set by docs/dev/issue_rules.md and phase item S0-17 in docs/dev/Implementation_plan.md, which is what this href names. Recorded plainly rather than inventing a plan document to satisfy the field.

results.title: Threat model and security architecture review of the design of record, revision 3
results.description: Re-review of docs/01 through docs/10 as of 2026-09-20, after #30 made the UUIDv5 key grammar normative. Nine findings, TM-1 through TM-9, recorded in docs/compliance/threat-model.md. No finding is new in this revision and none was invalidated: #30 strengthened TM-6 by making the party-not-in-key rule and the consumer-side deduplication requirement normative in docs/03-data-model.md rather than stated only in the threat model. TM-6 stands, because writing a rule down is not enforcing it. None of the nine is marked mitigated, which remains the correct result for a repository with no application code. This revision also fixes the cadence: during a phase whose deliverables are the contracts this document reasons about, a trigger firing is logged in the interim staleness ledger and the attestation is re-issued at phase exit rather than per merge. The triggers themselves are not narrowed.

control-selections.description: Developer testing and evaluation — threat modeling and vulnerability analyses.

observations.title: Threat model re-reviewed and attested after the UUID key grammar became normative, and the re-issue cadence fixed
observations.description: The threat model was re-reviewed against the design of record following #30, which made the UUIDv5 key grammar normative. The review added no finding and invalidated none; it strengthened TM-6, whose two requirements are now stated normatively in the data model. Decisions across the nine are unchanged: one deferred as an open phase-0 decision (TM-4, the chain head has no anchor outside the writer's control), one accepted and inherited (TM-8, deployment), one accepted risk within TM-5, and the rest carried as requirements on the phases that build the affected component. The revision exists because the cadence rule itself is written in the attested document, so recording it changes the document and therefore requires a new record.

relevant-evidence.description: The threat model at revision 3, hashed in back-matter.
The attestation this supersedes, and the hash of the revision it reviewed.

observations.remarks: Expiry is unchanged from r2 and is 180 days from the substantive review on 2026-09-19, not 180 days from this re-issue. Resetting the clock on each revision would turn a bounded interval into a perpetual one. It also goes stale early, before that date, on a change to the trust boundary, the evidence chain order, the signing or canonicalisation scheme, how roles are derived from documents, the isolation of what-if overlays, the federation's peer verification or UUID key grammar, or on the first release serving real projections to an Authorizing Official. While phase P0 is open those triggers are logged in the interim staleness ledger and folded in at phase exit, because P0's deliverables are the contracts this document reasons about and the grammar trigger therefore fires for most of the phase. A firing that contradicts a finding or invalidates a stated assumption re-issues immediately regardless. Completing a phase is not itself a trigger.
